question: Why are tummy (gastrointestinal) problems considered dangerous if they aren't treated early?

options.A: They almost always resolve without treatment
options.B: They only impact the outer skin layers
options.C: They rarely affect other body organs
options.D: They can quickly cause systemic body crises

explanation: Great job thinking this through! Because your digestive tract is closely linked to your body's fluid and immune systems, a local tummy issue can easily spread and affect your whole body. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h1)

question: As a nurse, why do you need to monitor patients with digestive disorders very closely?

options.A: Digestive issues never change after admission
options.B: Intestinal tracts do not connect to other systems
options.C: The gut controls vital fluid and acid-base balance
options.D: Patients with gut problems refuse all medication

explanation: Spot on! The gut manages critical body functions like fluids and chemistry. When things go wrong there, the whole body feels it. You are getting the hang of this! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h1)

question: A patient has been vomiting heavily for hours. Which acid-base imbalance are they most likely to develop?
explanation: You've got this! Throwing up clears out hydrochloric acid from the stomach, leaving the blood more alkaline (basic) than normal. Chemistry in action! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h2)

question: Which electrolyte level drops rapidly when a patient suffers from severe, ongoing diarrhea?
explanation: Well done! Lower GI fluids are packed with potassium. When diarrhea flushes them out quickly, the patient loses too much potassium, leading to hypokalemia. Every question makes you sharper! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h2)

question: What is a classic, tell-tale sign of bleeding in the upper part of the gastrointestinal tract?

options.A: Bright red lower rectal bleeding only

explanation: Spot on! As blood travels down and gets digested through the upper GI tract, it changes color and texture, resulting in dark, sticky stools known as melena. You're learning clinical signs like a pro! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h3)

question: What is the primary danger when a bleeding patient slips into hypovolemic shock?

options.A: The body produces too much red blood
options.C: Vital organs are starved of oxygen

explanation: Exactly right! Losing too much blood means the heart doesn't have enough fluid to pump oxygen to major organs like the brain, heart, and kidneys. Clinical thinking looks great on you! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h3)

question: You are assessing a patient's abdomen and suspect peritonitis. Which physical sign would you expect to find?

options.C: Cool and moist skin on the arms

explanation: Brilliant! When the lining of the belly gets irritated by leaked digestive juices or stool, the muscle wall tightens up stiffly to protect itself. You're building solid assessment skills! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h4)

question: Why can a blocked intestine (bowel obstruction) eventually lead to a tear or perforation?

options.A: Trapped pressure cuts off the blood supply to the wall
options.B: The liver swells and crushes the intestines
options.C: Digestive enzymes dissolve the outside of the skin
options.D: Patients eat too much roughage while blocked

explanation: You nailed it! As contents pile up behind a blockage, the pressure squeezes the blood vessels in the intestinal wall until the tissue dies and tears. Physics and anatomy working together! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h4)

question: Which of these conditions is a direct result of the gut failing to absorb nutrients over a long period?
explanation: Spot on! If a damaged gut lining can't absorb key minerals like iron, the body simply can't manufacture enough healthy red blood cells. Keep up the fantastic work! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h5)

question: How does long-term protein deficiency affect a patient who is trying to recover from an illness?

options.A: It delays wound healing and lowers immunity
options.B: It causes blood pressure to rise rapidly
options.C: It makes the bones overly dense and thick
options.D: It speeds up recovery from infections

explanation: Correct! Proteins are the building blocks your body uses to repair tissues and build immune cells. Without enough protein, healing takes much longer. You are mastering nutritional nursing! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h5)

question: What toxin buildup is primarily responsible for causing hepatic encephalopathy in liver failure?
explanation: Well done! A struggling liver can't convert nitrogen waste into urea properly, letting ammonia pile up in the bloodstream and mess with brain function. You're crushing these patho questions! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h6)

question: What makes hepatorenal syndrome different from regular kidney failure?

options.A: Kidneys stop working because of high blood sugar
options.B: It only happens to people with healthy livers
options.C: It causes permanent physical damage to kidney tissue
options.D: The kidneys fail due to altered blood flow, not physical injury

explanation: Spot on! Hepatorenal syndrome happens because of severe blood circulation changes caused by liver issues—the kidney tissue itself isn't physically damaged at first. Excellent clinical insight! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h6)

question: What is one of the most important nursing duties when caring for a patient with a GI disorder?

options.B: Tracking exact fluid intake and output

explanation: You got it! Accurate fluid charts help nurses catch dangerous fluid losses or fluid buildup early when bleeding, vomiting, or diarrhea strike. Essential nursing care! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h7)

question: Your patient has a GI bleed. You notice their heart rate is rising and their blood pressure is falling. What does this most likely mean?

options.C: A sudden spike in blood sugar

explanation: Brilliant deduction! When blood volume drops, the heart beats faster to try and compensate, but eventually blood pressure drops as shock sets in. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h7)

question: Which supportive procedure is commonly used to give the bowel a rest during an acute GI crisis?
explanation: Spot on! An NG tube suctions out stomach contents and gas, which lets the bowel rest and prevents further pressure or vomiting. You are building up great practical knowledge! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h8)

question: Why is fast teamwork among healthcare staff so essential when managing GI complications?

options.A: Conditions can deteriorate into life-threatening emergencies very quickly
options.B: Nurses are not allowed to touch patients without a doctor present
options.C: Medical staff must share paperwork equally among themselves
options.D: Collaborative care guarantees that surgery will never be needed

explanation: You got it! Emergencies like bowel tears or massive bleeding move fast, meaning the team has to act together instantly to keep the patient safe. Teamwork makes the dream work in nursing! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h8)
